newsitem.title: PERU: Bank of Canada says not worried by Canadian dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada says not worried by Canadian dollar.

text.p: Canada is not worried about the weakness of its dollar and trusts market forces will eventually help it recover ground again, Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Timothy Noel said Thursday.
"Markets tend to find reasonable trading levels over time but from time to time you'll get some volatily and maybe some overshooting," he said. "That is the nature of the markets."

He told Reuters in Lima, where he is taking part in a central bankers' meeting, that his government was not considering raising interest rates or taking any other immediate action to prop up its currency.
"The bank does not want to react to every wiggle in the dollar," he said. He said it would only consider rising rates if the country's overall monetary conditions were appropriate.

Canada's dollar weakened to a two-year low on Friday amid concern the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates in May, weighing further on the Canadian dollar and pushing the Bank of Canada to raise rates. But it rebounded this week and Thursday afternoon was trading at 1.3919/24 per U.S. dollar.

Noel also stressed that it was still strong against other major currencies such as the mark and the yen and that he trusted market perceptions of the country's fundamentals -- including low inflation, a decreasing government deficit and an improving trade deficit -- would help prop it up.
"There is no question that the market feels that the Canadian dollar is undervalued from a medium-term perspective," he said. He would not speculate on when the dollar might recover ground again.
